children: Australian shares ended lower on Thursday, with broad-based losses outweighing gains in energy stocks, after a mixed jobs report did little to alter market expectations that the central bank will raise interest rates next week.
fell 0.7% to 8,702, its lowest close in more than a week.

Data showed net employment rose 39,500 in August from July, topping forecasts, while the jobless rate beat expectations and rose to a five-year high of 4.6%, but within a range that the Reserve Bank of Australia governor had said could help combat inflation.

"This jobs report reinforces the view that the Australian labour market is cooling rather than cracking, which supports the RBA's inflation-fighting stance while keeping hopes of a soft landing alive," said Greg Smith, investment specialist at Generate Investment Management.
Swaps imply a 95% chance the central bank will lift its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.60% at its September 28-29 meeting.

A single month's data is unlikely to convince the RBA that inflation risks have faded, with the focus after September shifting to whether unemployment continues to rise and  inflation moderates accordingly, Smith said.
